_about: Configuration for scripts/verify-skills.py (SKILL-G).
Copy this file to docs/governance/skill-policy.json and edit it. The copy is
project-owned: the harness never manages it, so your edits are not drift.
Keys starting with _ are ignored by the gate.
skills_root  the installed skill tree(s). One string or a list. The release
fans out into every selected target root, so list the roots you
installed. A listed root that does not exist is skipped, which
is how selecting a subset of targets stays quiet.
skills       ONLY skills the receipt does not own — normally your own local
ones. Core and profile skills are read from .harness.lock, which
already records the layer of each, so restating them here would
be a second copy of the same fact and the first thing to rot when
a profile selection changes. Naming a receipt-owned skill is
allowed but must agree with the lock.
local   authored by this project; must be covered by a lock
override and must not be receipt-owned.
The gate fails on any skill present on disk that neither the lock nor this
file accounts for, so a hand-copied skill tree cannot drift in silently.
POLICY-G (scripts/verify-policies.py) compares this copy against the
example the release ships. When a release adds a key here, your copy does
not gain it — the harness never edits a project-owned file — so the gate
reading it would treat the capability as unconfigured and report clean.
POLICY-G turns that silence into a finding.
To decline a key deliberately, list its name in "_declined": ["key"].
Declining is a decision and leaves a trace; not knowing is neither.
